newsitem.title: UK: Harrisons current food/agri profits down.
newsitem.headline: Harrisons current food/agri profits down.

text.p: British diversified group Harrisons & Crosfield Plc said on Tuesday that operating profits at its food and agriculture division were "down sharply" in the four months to April 1997.

Chairman George Paul told shareholders at the company's annual meeting that food and agriculture profits have been dragged lower by a continuing shortfall in cattle feed sales and poor trading conditions at subsidiary Pauls Malt.
The company said it was in the process of evaluating a range of options to maximise its future growth prospects and enhance shareholder value.
It noted that profits in its chemical and industrial division were virtually unchanged in the current four month period against a year ago.
Harrisons said that with the exception of its joint venture Akcros, its chemicals businesses are ahead of last year "in almost all areas".
"Profits would have been better still but for the strength of sterling," said Paul.
Elsewhere, sales at Harcros, part of its timber and building supplies division, were up 15 percent in the first four months and operating profits were ahead, said the company.

Paul also told shareholders that he planned to retire after 12 years with the group, first as chief excutive and then chairman. He will continue working until a new chairman from outside the group has been appointed, probably towards the end of summer.
